To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the GVH reaction observed in lpr→+/+ bone marrow chimeras is caused by the lysis of lpr→+/+, not lpr→lpr, lymphocytes, and is not due to alloantigens.
the lpr mutation causes a defect in immunoregulatory mechanisms which results in a nonspecific T‐cell activation in the host.
the lpr mutation is not responsible for GVH‐like reactions observed in congenic recipients of lpr BM, but rather that the lpr BM causes nonspecific activation of mature T cells in +/+ recipients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of autoimmunity in a murine model, the lpr mutant mouse, in which the disease is caused by the expression of a gene mutation.
the mechanisms of immune regulation and tolerance in autoimmune disease.
the development of an animal model of chronic graft‐vs.-host (GVH)-like disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the chronic GVH syndrome observed after lpr/lpr → +/+ BM transfer is due to the functional defect associated with lpr/lpr cells rather than due to alloantigenic difference between lpr/lpr and +/+ cells.
lpr/lrp→+/+ BM transfer causes a GVH reaction in +/+ but not in lrp/lrp recipients because of intrinsic defects in the lrp/lrp immune system.
the lpr mutation causes a defect in immunoregulatory mechanisms that leads to nonspecific T‐cell activation and autoantibody production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lpr/lpl→+/+ BM chimera model is a model for GVH‐like disease.
the lpr mutation is associated with an immunoregulatory disturbance that leads to nonspecific activation and expansion of T cells.
we have found that there is a functional defect in lpr/l pr BM cells that is expressed after transfer to normal irradiated mice, which results in an increase in IgG levels and a GVH‐ like response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lpr→+ chimeras develop a GVH‐related syndrome because of the lpr gene, and not because of the H‐2 difference between the lpr and + strains.
the lpr mutation does not cause GVH‐like disease by itself, but rather by causing an immunoregulatory disturbance which leads to nonspecific activation and expansion of T cells.
alloantigen differences are not responsible for GVH‐like responses observed after lpr/lpr → +/+ BM chimerism.
